title: Does a G1 humanoid on a drive-and-lift base nail a 4x8 sheet faster than a walking G1?
summary: Takes the 13-stance cover of buildbot-stance (62 nails, reach 0.3 m, 50 N push) and replaces its swept re-stance time with one computed from a drive speed (0.2–1.0 m/s) and a lift speed (0.05–0.5 m/s) plus a 0 or 2 s settle, with the stances visited in the exact shortest order (Held-Karp). The 12 moves cost 5–63 s and the sheet takes 54–121 s (nailing 25 s at a 4 m/s tip, 59 s at 0.5 m/s), against 85–119 s for a walking G1 at 5 s per step and 372 s by hand. Matching the 61 s gantry needs the fast tip, a 0.5 m/s drive and a 0.2 m/s lift; lift speed matters more than drive speed, and settling dominates once the base is quick. Drive, lift and settle are swept, not taken from a chosen machine (a JLG scissor-lift listing is quoted unverified); the G1 reach is carried over unchanged from static statics, with no sway, vibration or base mass, and the stance cover minimises count, not time.
lede: does a G1 on a drive-and-lift base nail a 4x8 sheet faster than a walking G1? Yes in 22 of 24 speed settings: 54-121 s a sheet (13 stances, 12 moves of 5-63 s) against 85-119 s walking and 372 s by hand, and it matches a 61 s gantry only with a fast tip, 0.5 m/s drive and 0.2 m/s lift (speeds swept, not a chosen machine; reach unchanged from static statics).
